title: PHASE A SAMPLING THE NEUTRAL DENSITY OF THE LOWER THERMOSPHERE - EXPRO+
description: Objectives and TasksThe activity aims to reach a preliminary design for a dedicated mission that will measure in-situ the neutral density, and when feasible the ion density as well, in very low-Earth orbit, i.e. the lower thermosphere below 250km and if feasiblebelow 200km, from aneccentric orbit with high inclination. The eccentricity shall be tuned to ensure orbital lifetimes spanning a significant part of the solar cycle and the high inclination shall ensure the capture of samples across the dynamic atmospheric regions that affect the majority of current spacecraft and can support the new generation of VLEO satellites.To couple in-situ measurements that can be used to calibrate atmosphere models in the region of interest with space safety applications such as improved orbital lifetime estimation of collision avoidance risk assessment, direct coupling with the mission dragprofiles is needed. Therefore, the mission shall embark an accelerometer and optimise its shape and AOCS control to facilitate precise orbit determination.Very low perigee orbits, with apogee still in low Earth orbit, are a challenge for space surveillance and tracking systems due to limited visibility from individual sensors and the orbit being highly affected by drag. The mission shall function as a calibration target for commercial tracking solution in Europe, to demonstrate the accuracy of their products against a ground truth provide by the mission in support of safely operating in the VLEO regime.To prepare for the above-described mission, the proposed activity will assess the overall feasibility of the mission and specifically include: Mission and requirements definition: redefine in detail the purpose and mission objectives deriving consistently the satellite system, the orbital, and the groundsegment requirements. These shall be derived from the identified need of performing orbital lifetime calculation and collision avoidance processes below 300km. Conceptual design: based on the mission definition and system requirements, a conceptual design of the satellite will be developed. This includes the basiclayout of the satellite, the platform mass and size, the orbit, the major components and subsystems considering as well launch vehicle, and groundsegment. Definition of the payload (e.g. mass spectrometers, accelerometers). Identify all critical items (< TRL 6) and derive technology development plans for each including definition of the VV approach. Given the eccentric orbit crossing highly utilised space traffic reason, perform a trade-off in platform manoeuvrability needs to extend the mission duration while managing collusion risk in accordance with ESA's space debris mitigation requirements. Preliminary cost and schedule: estimate of costs and schedules is developed based on the conceptual design, and the system requirements to be below 25MEUR. Risk assessment: risks associated with the mission and satellite design will be identified, evaluated, and assessed. Feasibility analysis: the feasibility of the mission and satellite design is assessed, taking into account technical, cost, and schedule considerations. Analysis of the commercialisation opportunities related to the mission concept and the related technologies.

title: S2-LT-04 + S2-LT-05 DEMONSTRATION OF THE OPERATIONAL CAPABILITY, ROBUSTNESS ENHANCEMENT AND MARKET READINESS OF NETWORKED LASER DEBRIS TRACKING - EXPRO +
description: The activity aims to mature and expand the Debris Laser Tracking Network toward operational readiness and market applicability. It focuses on improving automation, system performance, product accuracy, and end-user alignment, while also addressing legal and regulatory constraints for compliant laser ranging operations, including potential ranging to active satellites.The network will be expanded by integrating at least one additional Satellite Laser Ranging station, upgraded to support debris laser ranging also during daytime, to improve station automation, and to interface with the DLTN automation framework.A coordinated observation campaign, involving end users and the ESA Laser Ranging Station, will validate the enhanced operational concepts, demonstrate improved network performance, and assess the benefits of simultaneous operations across multiple debris ranging stations. The activity will deliver technical notes, market concepts, observation data, software, and station hardware upgrades over an 18-months contract period

title: JOINT IMPLEMENTATION OF SAT-3 AND COGNITIVE CLOUD COMPUTING IN SPACE (EOCOGNITIVELAB)
description: EOCognitiveLab brings together the evolution of the sat mission series and ESA's work on Cognitive Cloud Computing in Space for Earth Observation (3CS4EO). The activity is intended to demonstrate the added values unlocked by AI-enabled, cooperative Earth Observation capabilities across multiple heterogeneous?satellites?(including, event-based acquisition replanning, coordinated acquisitions), onboard processing and inter-satellite-link information exchange,?for selected end-to-end Earth Observation use cases, and to establish an in-orbit laboratory for autonomous, distributed and software-defined Earth Observation missions.?  The mission will be based on a cooperative two-satellite space segment, equipped with onboard computing capabilities, supported by ground processing, and an exploitation platform enabling data distribution and community access. In addition, EOCognitiveLab will leverage open inter-satellite-link interfaces and be designed to support future expansion through the federation of additional Earth Observation missions.? As an in-orbit laboratory, EOCognitiveLab will provide an open and expandable environment for additional in-orbit experimentation forESA Members, Associated and Cooperating States EO community. Target experimentation areas include cooperative sensing, distributed processing, novel mission-orchestration approaches, onboard federated learning and fine-tuning, and other AI techniques relevant to distributed Earth Observation systems.?  The proposed?activity will be implemented through a Mission Consolidation Phase followed, subject to a successful Gate Review, by a Mission Implementation Phase covering detailed design, development, integration, verification, launch, LEOP, commissioning and in-orbit verification up to the In-Orbit Commissioning Review.

title: MINIATURIZATION OF NITROGEN-VACANCY CENTER-BASED MAGNETOMETERS - EXPRO+
description: Objective:  To develop a space proven NV-Centred Diamond magnetometer with reduced SWaP. Description:  Magnetic field measurements from low Earth orbit are important for understanding Earth's magnetosphere, monitoring of space weather, and studying geophysical processes. These measurements provide insights into solar-terrestrial interactions and help mitigate risks to both orbital infrastructure and terrestrial systems. NV -centres magnetometers are recent developments that have been successfully implemented on the ISS. Next to their scientific interest, one of their applications lays in using the magnetic field for AOCS purposes in space. Using a magnetic map, the full attitude of the spacecraft can be followed. This has been demonstrated during the first Ariane launch where one of these systems could follow the first minutes of the trajectory of the rocket. There is now the need to further develop such system to allow them to be utilized for navigation of spacecrafts or on other bodies (which have a magnetic field) with a specific focus on reduction of size and mass of the instrument to be integrated to AOCS system. The development shall be focused on miniaturisation and reduction of resources and on increasing the resolution of the magnetometers to pT.  This activity encompasses the following tasks:  - Consolidation of technical requirements given application in miniature quantum devices and preliminary design.- Detailed design of the magnetometer. - Manufacturing, integration and functional verification. - Test campaign, outcomes and development plan to qualification. Deliverables: Breadboard, Reports
